Misoprostol, a prostaglandin analog, is indicated for the prevention and treatment of NSAID-induced ulcers as it provides mucosal protection and reduces gastric acid secretion. The reasoning chains supporting Misoprostol's role in preventing ulcers due to chronic NSAID use are consistent with medical consensus. analysis: Chronic use of NSAIDs is known to lead to peptic ulcer disease due to the inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, which diminishes the protective mucosal barrier in the gastrointestinal tract. Misoprostol, a prostaglandin analog, is specifically indicated for the prevention and treatment of NSAID-induced ulcers as it not only provides mucosal protection but also reduces gastric acid secretion. While Esomeprazole is effective in reducing gastric acid and can be used in the management of ulcers, it is not the first-line treatment specifically for NSAID-induced ulcers. The other options, Pirenzepine and Loratadine, are not relevant to the treatment of peptic ulcers. Therefore, based on the consensus in medical literature, Misoprostol is the most appropriate choice for treating peptic ulcer disease caused by chronic NSAID use.
